title: COVID-19 CT Lung and Infection Segmentation Dataset

authors.name: Jun Ma
authors.affiliation: Nanjing University of Science and Technology

authors.name: Deng Xueyuan
authors.affiliation: Chongqing University of Posts and Telecommunications

abstract: This dataset contains 20 labeled COVID-19 CT scans. Left lung, right lung, and infections are labeled by two radiologists and verified by an experienced radiologist. To promote the studies of annotation-efficient deep learning methods, we set up three segmentation benchmark tasks based on this dataset https://gitee.com/junma11/COVID-19-CT-Seg-Benchmark. In particular, we focus on learning to segment left lung, right lung, and infections using pure but limited COVID-19 CT scans; existing labeled lung CT dataset from other non-COVID-19 lung diseases; heterogeneous datasets include both COVID-19 and non-COVID-19 CT scans.

narrative:
Short impact summary

The COVID-19 CT Lung and Infection Segmentation Dataset has become a widely used reference point for COVID-19 imaging research, with 240 citations in OpenAlex, 287 documented downstream reuses, and strong usage in Zenodo with 65,781 views and 50,288 downloads. Its impact is concentrated in computer vision and medical imaging workflows, especially segmentation, and it is repeatedly cited in articles, conference papers, and preprints across multiple countries and institutions.

Full narrative

Published in 2020 on Zenodo and released as an open-access dataset, this work provided 20 labeled COVID-19 CT scans with left lung, right lung, and infection annotations verified by radiologists. The dataset was explicitly designed to support annotation-efficient deep learning and segmentation benchmarking, which helps explain why it has functioned as infrastructure rather than as a one-off data release. The record shows sustained scholarly uptake: citations rose quickly after release, peaking in 2021 and 2022, and the citing literature spans journal articles, conference papers, and preprints.

The reuse profile reinforces that role. OpenAlex records 287 downstream reuses, including software, journal articles, conference papers, preprints, reviews, dissertations, and other scholarly outputs. The dataset is especially visible in venues and channels associated with fast-moving methodological work, including arXiv, medRxiv, Research Square, and journals such as Medical Image Analysis, Biomedical Signal Processing and Control, IEEE Access, and Computers in Biology and Medicine. The citing concepts cluster around COVID-19 diagnosis using AI, radiomics and machine learning in medical imaging, and medical image segmentation, showing that the dataset has been used primarily as a methodological benchmark for segmentation and related imaging tasks.

The geographic and institutional spread of the citing literature is broad, with notable activity in China, India, the United States, Iran, South Korea, Brazil, Germany, and Saudi Arabia. The institutional landscape is similarly diverse, spanning universities and medical centers across several regions. This pattern suggests that the dataset has been adopted as a shared technical resource in a global research response to COVID-19, especially in education and healthcare settings where imaging-based AI methods were being rapidly developed and tested.

Usage indicators also point to continued interest beyond formal citation. Zenodo reports more than 50,000 downloads and over 65,000 views, and the dataset is linked to an openly accessible repository environment with multiple open instances. Crossref data citations show early and continuing reuse in both posted content and journal articles, while scite records 45 mentioning works. Public-discourse archives were unavailable in the record, so the impact story here is best understood through scholarly reuse, repository usage, and the dataset’s role as a benchmark foundation for COVID-19 CT segmentation research.
